title: Hallucination as Constructibility Collapse: A Geometric Theory of LLM Factual Grounding KA Universality Program 2.0 — Paper P35
abstract: We propose that LLM hallucination is a manifestation of latent constructibility collapse (LCC) in the token- generation dynamics. The hidden-state trajectory defines a dynamical system whose pseudospectral margin measures the model’s sensitivity to perturbation at each generation step. When drops below a critical threshold — due to distributional drift, knowledge boundary crossing, or attention entropy explosion — the model loses its capacity to self-correct, and hallucination emerges. We formalize this connection through four results: (T1) the Hallucination–Collapse Correspondence, showing that factual grounding loss coincides with resolvent margin erosion in the hidden-state Jacobian; (T2) the Attention Entropy–Margin Coupling, proving that high attention entropy drives erosion; (T3) a Runtime Hallucination Detector based on monitoring along the generation trajectory; and (T4) a Constructibility-Governed Decoding strategy that modifies the sampling distribution when the margin drops below a safety threshold. We introduce two new objects: the Factual Grounding Margin and the Hallucination Risk Index , providing the first geometrically grounded, real-time hallucination diagnostic.

title: Transitive Taint Propagation for Shared Agent State: An Empirical Evaluation
abstract: The v0.2 companion measured Transitive Taint Propagation (TTP) — a primitive that records, at write time, the provenance dependencies of each write and contains the blast radius of a poisoned write without re-verifying the whole field — on a seeded synthetic oracle, and reported a first real-workload accuracy slice on one workload class and one model. The loudest open objection was generalization: does the result hold beyond a single model and a single agent topology, and is the self-declared ground truth it rests on actually sound? This version answers both with measurements on real instrumented agent traces. (1) Model-agnostic, measured: across three model families — Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and gemini-2.5-flash — the causal-derivation premise holds in all three and the read-relevance gate lifts blast-radius precision 80%→100% in the same threshold band for every family. (2) Topology-general, with an honest recall split: across six distinct agent topologies the gate reaches 100% precision in every one, with the recall cost reported per workload and falling exactly where the topology stresses the two published boundaries (cross-session carry; paraphrase floor). (3) Ground-truth integrity, measured per workload: under-declaration is ≈0% in five of six topologies but 50% in one (plan-execute), so it does not universally generalize and must be measured, never assumed. (4) Two instrumentation closures: an observable carry channel recovers a cross-session dependency edge from 33%→100% recall on a no-re-read handoff, and a retrieval-layer (logged-input) ground truth on plan-execute lifts measured precision 46.2%→88.5%. The precision gain generalizes; each of its costs is named and on the page. CC-BY-4.0.

title: A General-Purpose Predictive World Model
abstract: World models are considered advanced artificial intelligence (AI) systems capable of simulating and understanding the various dynamics of the real world. In fact, these models represent significant progress in AI, as they have established a new paradigm for learning compact, predictive representations that enable AI agents to reason, simulate, and act in complex environments. Despite this not being a new concept within the AI community, the main challenges lie in the existing implementation, which spans variational generative models, contrastive predictive methods, and imagination-based latent reinforcement learning, all of which remain completely fragmented in both design and theoretical understanding. It is on this basis that this paper proposes a generalised framework architecture that unifies representation learning, latent dynamics modelling, and policy optimisation within a single probabilistic design. The new architectural design proposes integrating generative objectives, including reconstruction and variational inference, with a predictive objective, namely contrastive and self-supervised learning. The whole idea in this case is to fully leverage structured latent states and imagination-based rollouts for efficient decision-making. Moreover, the motivation is that, by abstracting and synthesising key principles from related concepts and architectures, the proposed unified model formulation can provide a coherent foundation for analysing, designing, and extending world-model-based systems. Therefore, this study argues that the current unified perspective advances the development of scalable, data-efficient, and general-purpose agents capable of learning, predicting, and planning in high-dimensional, partially observable environments.

title: Long-Term Measurements of the Characteristics of a Fixed and Mobile Photovoltaic Installation
abstract: This paper analyzes the properties of two photovoltaic installations located in close proximity to each other. One is stationary, while the other abruptly changes the orientation of its panels, which follow the apparent daily movement of the Sun. Measurement results illustrating the daily variations in the productivity of both installations across four seasons are presented and discussed. The rationale for using a mobile installation on the analyzed days is demonstrated.

title: The AI Trust Gap
abstract: The chapter examines the widening divide between artificial intelligence use and trust. It highlights the rapid rise of intentional use across work and personal life while showing that confidence in artificial intelligence systems has steadily declined. The chapter explores why this gap persists, highlighting concerns about accuracy, cybersecurity, misinformation, job displacement and the opacity of automated systems. It shows how perceptions often outweigh lived experience, with many consumers worrying about risks they have not personally encountered. The chapter also explains how limited understanding of artificial intelligence’s role in everyday tools contributes to skepticism and why this disconnect matters for marketers and organizations. By mapping the psychological, cultural and structural forces shaping public sentiment, the chapter positions trust as a prerequisite for meaningful engagement. It establishes the foundation for understanding how consumers evaluate artificial intelligence and what they need to feel confident using it.

title: E-MRL: Cross-view Aligned Evidence-driven Multimodal Reinforcement Learning for Reliable 3D Tumor Analysis
abstract: While Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show great promise in volumetric medical report generation, they frequently suffer from visual hallucinations and a lack of grounding in 3D CT data. Current Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) strategies typically optimize text fidelity alone, essentially rewarding correct diagnoses derived from language priors rather than genuine visual perception. To address this, we propose cross-view aligned Evidence-driven Multimodal Reinforcement Learning (Evidence-MRL, noted as E-MRL), a reliable RL reasoning framework that formulates the generation process as a Markov Decision Process of "diagnosis-localization-verification". Unlike standard approaches, our model is explicitly trained to identify a "key evidence slice" alongside the global diagnostic report, grounding its findings in verifiable visual evidence. Crucially, we introduce a novel cross-view consistency reward, which validates the semantic alignment between the golden-standard report and a local visual re-query of the selected key slice, providing additional rewards for correctly-localized reasoning. Experiments on large-scale 3D CT tumor datasets demonstrate that E-MRL significantly reduces hallucinations and improves diagnostic accuracy compared to SFT and RL baselines, offering a clinically interpretable solution for visually-grounded and tumor analysis.

title: Acoustic Landmark Detector based on Conformer and HuBERT
abstract: Acoustic landmarks (abrupt acoustic changes tied to speech events) offer a linguistically grounded representation for speech analysis. We study automatic landmark detection with Conformer models, evaluating 14 configurations spanning architecture, loss, label representation, feature extractor, and data conditions on 1 839 manually annotated utterances with eight landmark types. We propose Gaussian soft labels with per-class temporal spread (sigma=10-20 ms), improving F1-at-20 ms by 7.0% absolute vs. hard labels by modeling annotation variability. Frozen HuBERT features perform best without fine-tuning (F1-at-20 ms=0.77). Stops and fricatives are reliable (F1>0.80), while vowels remain challenging (F1 approx 0.55). On our corpus, our system reaches a 13.8% Landmark Error Rate (LER). This is not directly comparable to AutoLandmark (31.3%) or SpeechMark (56.5%), evaluated on a different corpus and metric. Per-class trends show detectability increases with event abruptness, consistent with Stevens' theory.

title: RS-Gen: A Multi-Stage Agentic Framework for Reasoning and Search-Augmented Image Generation
abstract: Recent years have witnessed remarkable progress in image generation and editing, particularly regarding instruction following and visual fidelity. However, when handling ambiguous intentions, logical reasoning, and Out-of-Distribution (OOD) knowledge, existing image models often yield sub-optimal results due to a lack of deep reasoning capabilities and real-time external information. Although emerging unified understanding-and-generation models attempt to bridge this gap, they remain constrained by their intrinsic parameter scales and static knowledge gaps. Inspired by agentic paradigms, we propose RS-Gen: a plug-and-play, training-free, multi-stage image agentic framework. RS-Gen innovatively introduces a "Questioning-and-Solving" closed-loop mechanism to accurately identify logical issues and knowledge gaps, autonomously planning actions to bridge information deficits and execute deep logical reasoning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RS-Gen significantly expands the capability boundaries of foundational image generation and editing models. Specifically, on the WISE Verified and RISEBench benchmarks, RS-Gen yields substantial absolute performance gains of 0.313 for Qwen-Image and 19.70 for Qwen-Image-Edit-2511, respectively, successfully elevating both to the state-of-the-art (SOTA) level among open-source models.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Learning for Enzyme-Substrate Interaction Prediction Under Low-Homology Shift
abstract: Enzyme substrate interaction (ESI) prediction is a fundamental computational task for biocatalyst discovery and reaction screening in large biochemical spaces. In practical settings, ESI prediction is challenged by sparse positive supervision and low-homology distribution shift, where test enzymes share limited sequence identity with those observed during training. To address these challenges, we propose RAMMESI, a retrieval-augmented multimodal framework for robust ESI prediction. RAMMESI learns explicit pairwise enzyme-substrate representations through directional cross-modal interaction modeling and adaptive fusion. To enhance robustness, RAMMESI retrieves neighboring enzymes at inference time, recombines them with the query substrate, and aggregates the resulting pairwise predictions as contextual evidence. To improve learning under sparse positive supervision, we further adopt an imbalance-aware weighted-BCE objective. Experiments on two ESI benchmarks under sequence-identity-aware splits demonstrate that RAMMESI achieves consistently strong performance, with particular advantages in more challenging low-identity regimes. In addition, the retrieval module improves multiple ESI backbones in a plug-and-play manner, suggesting that retrieval provides a general mechanism for improving robustness under homology shift.

title: Quantum Bayesian Time Series Forecasting with Uncertainty Quantification
abstract: This study thoroughly evaluates a Quantum Bayesian Time Series Forecasting model, focusing on how well it can measure uncertainty in different types of noise and with varying numbers of data points. The paper compared the model‘s performance using several key metrics” Mean Squared Error (MSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Coverage at 95%, Aleatoric and Epistemic uncertainty” against both synthetic noise models (heteroscedastic, heavy-tailed, homoscedastic, and regime-dependent) and real financial data. The results highlighted quantum advantages in breaking down uncertainty, especially in situations where data is volatile or not stable over time. Using a Bayesian time series model, the study obtained average levels of aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty for each assumption at different forecast sample sizes ”60-, 120-, 180-, and 240- time units (which can be years). The heavy-tailed error model performed best, with the lowest MSE and MAE across many sample sizes, such as MSE of 1.71 at sample size 60 and a high coverage of 0. The regime-dependent model performed well in one situation (lowest MSE of 1). The paper showed that including heavy-tailed errors and accounting for regime changes improved the accuracy and reliability of Bayesian forecasts. These results suggested that both aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty should be modelled in time series data, as done in full predictive density approaches, and have important implications for forecasting in financial, economic, or environmental contexts where volatility and sudden changes are common.Keywords: Bayesian; Quantum Computing, Simulation; Time Series; Forecasting

title: Sentiment Analysis of Google Maps Reviews on Temple Tourism in Central Java Using IndoBERT Embeddings and BiLSTM
abstract: The rapid growth of user-generated content provides valuable insights into tourists’ perceptions of destinations. This study analyzes sentiment in Google Maps reviews of temple tourism destinations in Central Java using IndoBERT embeddings and a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) model. A total of 10,714 Indonesian-language reviews were collected through web scraping and processed through preprocessing, pseudo-labeling, embedding generation, and model training. To prevent data leakage, the dataset was divided into stratified training and testing sets, while Random OverSampling (ROS) was applied only to the training data. Since manually annotated labels were unavailable, sentiment categories were generated automatically using a pre-trained IndoBERT classifier. The BiLSTM model achieved 80.25% accuracy on the imbalanced dataset and approximately 95% accuracy against IndoBERT-generated pseudo-labels under balanced training conditions. Improvements in Macro F1-score and balanced accuracy indicate better recognition of minority classes. However, the results should be interpreted cautiously because pseudo-labeling and oversampling may affect performance. Overall, this exploratory study demonstrates the potential of IndoBERT and BiLSTM for Indonesian tourism sentiment analysis while highlighting the need for human-annotated data and stronger validation in future research.

title: A FRAMEWORK FOR SEMANTIC DOCUMENT SIMILARITY DETECTION BASED ON AUTOMATIC TEXT SUMMARIZATION AND TRANSFORMER EMBEDDINGS
abstract: The rapid growth of digital document collections has increased the need for efficient methods for identifying semantically similar documents. Traditional similarity measures often rely on lexical overlap and fail to capture deeper semantic relationships. This paper proposes a framework for semantic document similarity detection based on automatic text summarization and transformer embeddings. First, source documents are summarized to extract their most informative content while reducing noise and redundancy. The generated summaries are then encoded using transformer-based embedding models to obtain semantic representations. Document similarity is computed in the embedding space using cosine similarity. The proposed approach improves retrieval efficiency and semantic matching accuracy for large-scale document collections

title: CREATION OF A DIGITAL CORPS OF UZBEKISTAN DIALECTS AND PHONETIC DESCRIPTION
abstract: This article analyzes the theoretical and practical issues of creating a digital corpus of Uzbek dialects and the principles of phonetic characterization of dialect materials. The processes of collecting, digitizing, transcribing and annotating dialect data are highlighted, and the importance of the phonetic corpus in linguistic research is substantiated. The possibilities of identifying and describing phonetic phenomena specific to Uzbek dialects based on corpus technologies are also shown. The results of the research can serve the development of Uzbek dialectology, corpus linguistics and computer linguistics.

title: An Enhanced Lightweight Encryption Method with Data Authentication in Internet of Things (IoT)
abstract: Ensuring safe and authenticated communication among resource-constrained devices is a major concern in the rapid growth of the Internet of Things (IoT) environment. In this paper, a lightweight cryptographic based encryption technique with authentication is proposed. Substitution-Permutation Network (SPN) structure provides a confidentiality and authentication mechanism that provides block level data integrity. Using Blum - Blum shub(BBS) and 2D trigonometric coupling chaotic map sequences are considered to generate the key values. Affine based substitution with circular shift permutation is considered to protect the data in IOT. Block-level data integrity is incorporated using an authentication mechanism. The results show that the designed method provides a high level of security with data integrity.

title: Predicting findings suggestive of aspiration pneumonia in Gram stained smears images of sputum
abstract: In this paper, first we newly introduce a finding suggestive of aspiration pneumonia in Gram stained smears images of sputum (a finding suggestive of AP, for short) as an image containing both polymicrobial patterns and phagocytotic patterns. Here, the polymicrobial pattern is a cluster consisting of both Gram positive and Gram negative bacteria and the phagocytotic pattern is a leukocyte enclosing bacteria as avoiding to its nucleus, representing a phagocytosis of bacteria by a leukocyte. Then, we predict findings suggestive of AP by applying two methods of an image classification and an object detection to Gram stained smears images of sputum.

title: Alternative syntaxes
abstract: The Crystallographic Information Framework provides both a concrete file syntax and an ontology of concepts characterized by specific data names in a family of dictionaries. While the concrete syntax is familiar to crystallographic applications, interoperability requires exchange of information using file syntaxes used in other scientific domains. A full specification is given for CIF-JSON, a JSON schema that affords a clean mapping of CIF semantic data into a well-supported serialization syntax. Several other syntax models are also described, allowing data exchange with macromolecular (PDBML, mmJSON, BinaryCIF) and chemical (CML, MIF) structural sciences. The semantics of the contained data are conserved through mappings of the data names with associated definitions in CIF dictionaries.

title: Memory-Native Non-Terrestrial Networks for Embodied Intelligence
abstract: Non-terrestrial networks (NTN) provide ubiquitous connectivity for embodied intelligence (EI), enabling robots in the wilderness to leverage cloud resources or report critical information to remote centers. However, the synergy is nontrivial due to the highly dynamic, resource-constrained, topology-varying, and task-oriented environment. Existing memoryless NTN protocols become inefficient, since the decisions are driven by local channel conditions and instantaneous service demands. To address these limitations, this paper proposes the memory-native NTN (Mem-NTN) paradigm that leverages long-horizon contexts for memory-augmented system optimization. To realize this paradigm shift, we establish a dual-memory architecture that distinguishes between physical memory representing the state of the world and digital memory encoding historical network experience. We develop memory acquisition, compression, valuation, update, and utilization mechanisms that facilitate cross-layer, memory-native decision-making, spanning from the physical and access layers up to the network and application layers. Experiments in satellite embodied question answering (SEQA) demonstrate that the proposed Mem-NTN consistently outperforms conventional stateless NTN and terrestrial approaches.

title: Complex Autonomous UAV Task Execution and Decision-Making With s(CASP)
abstract: Autonomous unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) must operate safely in dynamic environments and adapt to changing mission conditions. Although deep learning approaches have shown strong performance for navigation and perception, they are often difficult to explain, verify, and modify for safety-critical tasks. We propose a symbolic state-centered UAV agent using the s(CASP) answer set programming system, enabling autonomous task execution with constraint-based commonsense reasoning in a high-fidelity Unreal Engine 5 environment. We fully implement prior work on the VECSR-A system to support multi-step autonomous behaviors including navigation, search, debris detection, precision spraying, object transport, and inspection. The UAV reasons over environmental and spatial constraints, dynamically revising plans when tasks fail or data is insufficient. Because decisions are based on commonsense reasoning, they are guaranteed to be correct and explainable. We evaluate the feasibility of s(CASP) for UAV control in realistic simulated missions. Results show that our framework enables explainable, adaptive autonomy without retraining, handling complex constraint-aware decisions and dynamic task reevaluation.

title: An Open-Source LFSR-Based Stochastic Leaky Integrate-and-Fire Neuron in SkyWater 130 nm: Design, Stochastic Characterisation, and Rate Coding
abstract: Stochastic spiking neurons trade exact arithmetic for controlled randomness, lowering area and tolerating input noise, which suits event-driven edge hardware. We present a compact, configurable stochastic leaky integrate-and-fire neuron in standard-cell CMOS on the SkyWater 130 nm process, released openly. A 16-bit configurable-polynomial linear-feedback shift register drives an eight-entry programmable activation table that sets a Bernoulli firing probability, and a saturating 16-bit leaky integrator with a programmable threshold and a refractory period of zero to seven cycles produces the spike train. All parameters are set through a sixteen-register serial interface, and the neuron runs from parallel inputs or entirely from the register file. From a model checked bit-exact against the register-transfer code, the period is 65535 states for a maximal-length polynomial and 63 for the shipped default, the eight-bit comparison value is uniform over the full period, and the per-entry firing probability equals the table value divided by 256. We also characterise a property a system-level model would not expose: the comparator output is serially correlated at short lags, with a negative lobe near lag eight, because the compared byte shifts by one bit each cycle; subsampling every sixteen cycles restores whiteness. Rate-coding sweeps show monotonic control of the output rate by the input weight and the threshold, and the refractory period caps the rate at one spike per refractory-plus-one cycles. The neuron occupies about 10,600 square micrometres at 70 per cent utilisation on a single Tiny Tapeout tile, meets 50 MHz timing with positive margin, and passes eighteen directed cocotb tests at register-transfer and gate level. All results are pre-silicon, from simulation and the open flow. The neuron is an openly released companion to a four-block neuromorphic suite reported separately.

title: SPADE: Structure-Prior Adaptive Decision Estimation
abstract: Physical-structure priors such as conservation laws, Hamiltonian forms, and symmetries can improve scientific machine learning when correct, but can degrade predictions when misspecified. Existing methods usually enforce a chosen structure or tune a soft penalty, without a calibrated rule for deciding whether to impose a prior, how strongly to impose it, which prior to use, or which subset of candidate laws holds. We introduce SPADE, Structure-Prior Adaptive Decision Estimation, a closed-form framework that treats this problem as shrinkage of the structure-violating block of an unconstrained estimator. SPADE uses one exact specification test and one estimand: the test decides whether the prior is supported by data, Stein-unbiased James-Stein shrinkage sets the enforcement strength with an $O(σ^2/n)$ oracle guarantee, and a gate commits to the hard prior only when the test certifies it. The same test yields consistent nested structure selection and Benjamini-Hochberg control for subset discovery in non-nested constraint families. Across a linear-subspace prior, a reservoir conservation law, and a nonlinear Hamiltonian prior on Duffing dynamics, SPADE tracks the oracle, beats a neural-network baseline, reduces correct-prior regret from $10.3\%$ to $2.6\%$, matches cross-validation with $1/71$ of the solves, selects the correct structure with $100\%$ accuracy, and recovers partial laws with controlled false relaxation.

title: Boosting Neural Video Codec via Scale-Driven Online Flow Refinement
abstract: Although state-of-the-art neural video codecs (NVCs) have achieved remarkable performance, they suffer from limited generalization when encountering complex motion patterns unseen during training. To bridge this domain gap without the expensive cost of online fine-tuning, we propose a Training-Free Scale-Driven Online Flow Refinement (SOFR) method. Serving as a plug-and-play module, SOFR integrates motion information from coarse and fine scales and dynamically fuses them according to warping accuracy, effectively rectifying motion estimation errors with negligible computational overhead. Furthermore, we design a rate-aware strategy that selects different dynamic fusion strategies according to bitrate modes, and employs a reliability check based on warping error to ensure robustness. Extensive experiments on the USTC-TD dataset verify the effectiveness and generalization of SOFR across various NVC frameworks, including DCVC-SDD, DCVC-FM, and EHVC. Notably, it brings an average of 2.84% and 4.05% bitrate savings in terms of PSNR and MS-SSIM, respectively, to DCVC-FM with negligible coding time increase. Our code is available at https://github.com/SunnyMass/SOFR.

title: A Parallel CUDA-based ABC heuristic with greedy decoding for the minimum independent dominating set problem
abstract: The Minimum Independent Dominating Set (MIDS) problem is an NP-Hard combinatorial optimization challenge with broad applications in wireless sensor networks and the Internet of Things (IoT). Due to the intractability of exact methods for large-scale graphs, approximate approaches are essential; however, the literature focuses primarily on sequential executions on the CPU. The objective of this work is to develop and evaluate a massively parallel Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) meta-heuristic, implemented in CUDA architecture with a greedy decoding strategy for the MIDS problem. The methodology encompassed a systematic literature review, an exploratory implementation of the Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm on the GPU, and the final development of the ABC algorithm using cooperative kernels mapped in a continuous vector space. Experimental results indicated that the ABC approach achieved speedup rates of up to 62.97x compared to its sequential version, also outperforming the parallel ACO model in both solution quality and execution time. When compared to the sequential state-of-the-art (drMIDS, ILPS3, and MAE-PB), the ABC in CUDA demonstrated high competitiveness, obtaining smaller sets across various instances in the order of milliseconds. It is concluded that massive parallelization combined with swarm intelligence is a robust and highly efficient solution, enabling complex optimizations in real-time for large-scale systems.

title: The Effects of Artificial Intelligence on Marketing Process Optimization: A Mixed-Methods Study using Thematic Analysis and Analytic Hierarchy Process
abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed business environments and created new opportunities for optimizing marketing processes. This study aims to investigate and prioritize the effects of AI on marketing process optimization, with a particular focus on improving operational efficiency, decision-making accuracy, customer experience, and organizational competitiveness. A mixed-methods approach was employed, combining thematic analysis of semi-structured interviews with 13 experts in marketing and information technology and the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to evaluate and rank the identified themes. The findings reveal that AI significantly enhances marketing processes by reducing operational and advertising costs, minimizing human errors, improving decision-making quality, accelerating marketing activities, and enabling personalized customer interactions. Among the identified factors, the reduction of human error emerged as the most influential effect, whereas resource management improvement received the lowest priority. The results further indicate that AI can strengthen firms’ competitive advantage and improve marketing effectiveness; however, its successful implementation requires careful management of privacy concerns and the development of strategies aligned with local cultural and market conditions. Overall, the study highlights AI as a strategic enabler of marketing process optimization and sustainable business performance.

title: Few-Shot Classification of C. elegans Developmental Stages via Explainable Hierarchical Hyperbolic Graph Embeddings
abstract: Abstract Automated, accurate, and fast developmental-stage classification of C. elegans from microscopy-based morphological images is essential for aging research, drug screening, and disease modeling. However, it remains challenging due to morphological similarities between stages and the limited annotated data. In this work, we propose HyperDev, a hyperbolic few-shot learning framework that addresses these limitations by directly encoding developmental hierarchies in the embedding space, unlike conventional Euclidean approaches that treat stages as independent classes. HyperDev uses Poincaré ball geometry, combined with a biologically informed developmental prior, to naturally represent stage relationships. We introduce our self-curated C. elegans dataset spanning seven developmental stages (Egg, L1–L4, Adult, Dauer) with extreme class imbalance (6-8 samples per minority class). HyperDev achieves competitive classification accuracy (76.9–88.3%) while providing intrinsic explainability across nine 7-way few-shot evaluation settings. The learned embeddings exhibited strong biological alignment (Pearson r = 0.669, p < 0.001), while significantly outperforming ProtoNet ( r = 0.187), MatchingNet ( r = 0.235), and RelationNet ( r = 0.464). These results establish hyperbolic geometry as a principled approach to explainable few-shot learning in biological imaging, where understanding learned representations is as critical as predictive performance. Clinical Relevance By enabling explainable, data-efficient developmental staging from scarce samples, HyperDev supports improved phenotype quantification for aging research, disease modeling, and drug screening.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) híbrido: arquiteturas, métodos de recuperação e desafios para sistemas baseados em large language models
abstract: O avanço dos Large Language Models (LLMs) transformou significativamente o campo do Processamento de Linguagem Natural, possibilitando aplicações em geração de texto, sistemas conversacionais, recuperação de informação e apoio à tomada de decisão. Apesar dos resultados expressivos alcançados, esses modelos ainda apresentam limitações relacionadas à atualização do conhecimento, rastreabilidade das fontes utilizadas e ocorrência de alucinações, caracterizadas pela geração de informações incorretas ou não verificáveis. Nesse contexto, a arquitetura Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) surgiu como uma abordagem capaz de integrar mecanismos de recuperação documental ao processo de geração textual, permitindo que respostas sejam fundamentadas em fontes externas atualizadas. Recentemente, arquiteturas híbridas passaram a combinar recuperação esparsa baseada em correspondência lexical e recuperação densa baseada em representações vetoriais semânticas, buscando maximizar a qualidade das evidências recuperadas. Este artigo apresenta uma revisão crítica da literatura sobre RAG híbrido, abordando seus fundamentos teóricos, principais arquiteturas, mecanismos de recuperação, estratégias de reranking, métodos de avaliação e desafios atuais. A análise da literatura demonstra que a integração entre BM25, Dense Retrieval e técnicas de reranking produz melhorias significativas em métricas como Recall@K, Mean Reciprocal Rank (MRR) e Faithfulness, além de reduzir a incidência de alucinações. Conclui-se que o RAG híbrido representa uma das abordagens mais promissoras para o desenvolvimento de sistemas inteligentes confiáveis, explicáveis e baseados em evidências.

title: Adapting Whisper for Sociophonetic Transcription
abstract: Presentation to the CorpusPhon2 workshop of the LabPhon20 conference in June 2026.Despite computational advancements, manual transcription remains a major bottleneck in sociophonetic data processing pipelines. Developments in Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) have the potential to substantially ease this bottleneck. OpenAI’s Whisper DNN ASR system (Radford et al., 2023) can be downloaded and run locally, making it suitable for data that cannot be uploaded to cloud-based services for privacy or consent reasons. Here, we use manually transcribed data from the QuakeBox (Clark et al., 2016) and Origins of New Zealand English (Gordon et al., 2007) corpora (QB and ONZE) to evaluate the suitability and adaptability of Whisper for generating initial sociolinguiscic transcripts of New Zealand English (NZE) audio. We encountered two main problems:Word ErrorsLabelling utterances with speaker IDs (diarization)To improve word errors we tried the following solutions, with some success:using a long --initial_prompt command line parameter with the original Whisper system (best error rate 9.9%)using CrisperWhisper (Zusag et al 2024), an extension of Whisper designed (among other things) to improve transcription of fillers (best error rate with our data: 11.7%)fine-tuning Whisper models using our own data (best error rate: 5.8%)To address the diarization, we evaluated WhisperX (Bain et al 2023), an extension of Whisper designed (among other things) to implement diarization. We found WhisperX to perform well, assigning speaker labels to utterances with 91-94% accuracy.Although the need for manual correction of resulting transcripts remains, the adapted Whisper model represents the foundations of an ASR pipeline that can produce serviceable, diarized, first-pass transcripts for sociophonetic analysis while addressing data privacy concerns. The specific models we adapted is most suited to NZE speech and the NZILBB transcription protocols, but its pipeline software are all open access and can be further adapted and modified by researchers to meet their own requirements.We are very grateful for the University of Canterbury's Research Compute Hub - DOI:10.18124/CANTERBURYNZ-UCRCH - for support with computing resources.

Here, we use manually transcribed data from the QuakeBox (Clark et al., 2016) and Origins of New Zealand English (Gordon et al., 2007) corpora (QB and ONZE) to evaluate the suitability and adaptability of Whisper for generating initial sociolinguiscic transcripts of New Zealand English (NZE) audio. We encountered two main problems:Word ErrorsLabelling utterances with speaker IDs (diarization)To improve word errors we tried the following solutions, with some success:using a long --initial_prompt command line parameter with the original Whisper system (best error rate 9.9%)using CrisperWhisper (Zusag et al 2024), an extension of Whisper designed (among other things) to improve transcription of fillers (best error rate with our data: 11.7%)fine-tuning Whisper models using our own data (best error rate: 5.8%)To address the diarization, we evaluated WhisperX (Bain et al 2023), an extension of Whisper designed (among other things) to implement diarization. We found WhisperX to perform well, assigning speaker labels to utterances with 91-94% accuracy.Although the need for manual correction of resulting transcripts remains, the adapted Whisper model represents the foundations of an ASR pipeline that can produce serviceable, diarized, first-pass transcripts for sociophonetic analysis while addressing data privacy concerns. The specific models we adapted is most suited to NZE speech and the NZILBB transcription protocols, but its pipeline software are all open access and can be further adapted and modified by researchers to meet their own requirements.We are very grateful for the University of Canterbury's Research Compute Hub - DOI:10.18124/CANTERBURYNZ-UCRCH - for support with computing resources.

title: A Synergized LLM-KG Framework for Domain Knowledge Cognition
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) evolve rapidly, yet their probabilistic generation is inherently nontraceable and leaves a persistent bottleneck in domain knowledge cognition.Retrieval augmentation via texts or knowledge-graphs (KGs) improves coverage and factual accuracy, but existing studies still depend largely on static knowledge structures and manually governed updating, so the obstacle to sustained and reliable domain knowledge cognition remains.This study therefore proposes a synergized LLM-KG framework for domain knowledge, centered on ontology-governed KG automatic generation (AutoGen) and update, and hybrid vector-graph retrieval for clause-grounded reasoning.Specifically, guided by a manually developed ontology, the KG is automatically constructed, incrementally enriched, and jointly used with vector retrieval to ground each query against both textual evidence and graph structure.A case study is conducted in construction contract management.Results demonstrate the robust KG AutoGen performance with average F1 scores of 0.904 for entity extraction and 0.856 for triple extraction.Across three query stages, the framework further improves multi-hop reasoning and clause-grounded accuracy, with its F1 advantage over GraphRAG widening from 0.00 to 0.37 and that over LLM-only prompting increasing from 0.25 to 0.45.This study provides a traceable route to deeper, more reliable, and continually refined domain knowledge cognition.

title: "PMSA-GAN: Semi-Supervised Multi-Scale Self-Attention GAN for Histopathology Segmentation in IoMT-Driven Consumer Healthcare"
abstract: "Early and accurate analysis of Hematoxylin andEosin (H&E)-stained histopathology images is critical for timelydiagnosis of lung and colon cancers, especially in modernconsumer-electronics-based healthcare ecosystems where medicaldata is increasingly captured, viewed, and processed on smartphones,tablets, and IoMT devices. However, limited labeledmedical datasets, high cellular variability, and cross-domaindistribution shifts make reliable segmentation challenging inreal-world CE environments. To address these issues, this paperproposes a Pseudo-Labeled Multi-Scale Self-Attention GAN(PMSA-GAN) for semi-supervised histopathology image segmentation.The model integrates Pseudo-Semi-Supervised learning(PSS) to enhance pseudo-label quality for unlabeled imagesfrom unknown distributions, combined with a multi-scale selfattentionmechanism and a semi-supervised GAN discriminatorfor improved pixel-level categorization. The proposed PMSAGANeffectively aligns with CE-centric biomedical applicationsby enabling high-accuracy segmentation with minimal annotateddata, making it suitable for deployment on resource-constrainededge\/consumer devices within IoMT ecosystems. Experimentson LC25000 and NCT-CRC-HE-100K datasets demonstrate thatPMSA-GAN outperforms existing baselines in accuracy, Dicescore, and AUC across 2%, 5%, and 20% labeled settings.By reducing annotation dependency and supporting privacypreservingedge\/IoMT processing, the proposed framework advancesthe integration of semi-supervised learning into nextgenerationconsumer electronics-driven personalized healthcare."

title: Long-term stability of quantum resources through gravitational cat states in a dissipative Markovian environment
abstract: The paradigm in which gravity can generate entanglement between distant masses represents a profound shift in our understanding of quantum-gravitational interfaces and is still among the active and debated topics. Recent work [A. ur Rahman , ] established gravitational cat states as robust carriers of quantum correlations under thermal and classical fields. In our work, we demonstrate their capacity to stabilize quantum resources under a dissipative environment, which is the dominant decoherence mechanism in engineered platforms such as superconducting qubits. By incorporating both gravitational-like and spin-orbit couplings in a Markovian open system, we analytically demonstrate that quantum correlations attain nonvanishing steady-state values, and the stationary fidelity is enhanced by increasing the gravitational-like coupling. The spin-orbit interaction drives Rabi-like oscillations that counteract monotonic decay, and the gravitational coupling mimics non-Markovian memory, enabling long-term information stability. These mechanisms position gravity-inspired interactions not merely as entanglement generators, but as active stabilizers of quantumness in realistic dissipative environments.

title: One Year Later...The Harms Persist, But So Do We!
abstract: General-purpose large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for mental health-related conversations, yet safety guardrails remain inadequate and inconsistent across clinical conditions. This study evaluates eight proprietary LLMs across 16 DSM-5 conditions using four adversarial attack variants, introducing an eight-dimension harm taxonomy and a multi-dimensional evaluation framework. Results show that safeguards hold reliably only for suicide and self-harm, while conditions such as eating disorders, substance use disorder, and major depressive disorder exhibit failure rates of up to 100%. We argue that ethical design and deployment of these LLMs demand clearly defined harm categories across clinical conditions and implementation of safeguards accordingly. Until such safeguards are in place, these models pose significant risks to vulnerable populations, making their growing integration into publicly available settings (e.g., schools, search engines, and consumer chatbots) are particularly concerning.

title: Equilibrium thermometry in the multilevel quantum Rabi model
abstract: The temperature sensitivity of a probe in equilibrium can be gauged by its thermal quantum Fisher information (QFI). It is known that probes exhibiting degeneracy in their energy-level structure can achieve larger sensitivities, while probes with a more uniform spectrum may remain sensitive over a broader temperature range. Here, we study the thermometric performance of a multilevel quantum Rabi model in which two well-separated atomic manifolds of near-degenerate levels couple to a single cavity mode. We generalize the standard quantum Rabi treatment in the adiabatic regime to find an approximate closed-form expression for the thermal QFI. We then characterize two complementary limits. On the one hand, a large dark-state manifold (dark-manifold saturation) produces a robust peak in thermal sensitivity due to bright-dark population transfer. Such increase in sensitivity is further maximized at an intermediate light-matter coupling strength. Maximizing instead the number of bright states (bright-manifold saturation) generates a broadband thermal response that becomes increasingly stable under random light-matter couplings as the number of levels is increased. The rich spectral structure of our cavity-QED model thus makes it a versatile and sensitive equilibrium thermometer over a broad range of temperatures.

title: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL GENERATIVA NO DIREITO: AUTORIA, PROTEÇÃO DE DADOS E GOVERNANÇA NO ENSINO JURÍDICO
abstract: O presente estudo teve como objetivo geral analisar os impactos jurídicos e pedagógicos da inteligência artificial generativa no campo do Direito, especialmente quanto à autoria de conteúdos produzidos por sistemas automatizados, ao tratamento de dados pessoais em modelos de processamento de linguagem natural e à necessidade de governança ética no ensino jurídico. Como objetivos específicos, buscou-se compreender a evolução conceitual da inteligência artificial, examinar os desafios da proteção autoral diante de obras produzidas com apoio de sistemas inteligentes, investigar os riscos relacionados ao uso de dados pessoais no treinamento de modelos de linguagem e analisar a necessidade de adaptação das práticas pedagógicas no ensino jurídico. A pesquisa foi desenvolvida por meio de revisão bibliográfica, com abordagem qualitativa, a partir de doutrinas, artigos científicos, legislação nacional e referências internacionais sobre inteligência artificial, direito autoral, proteção de dados e educação jurídica. O estudo evidenciou que o ordenamento jurídico brasileiro ainda apresenta lacunas relevantes no tratamento das criações geradas por inteligência artificial, especialmente porque a legislação autoral permanece centrada na figura humana do autor. Também se constatou que os modelos de processamento de linguagem natural dependem de grandes bases de dados, o que amplia riscos relacionados à privacidade, à reidentificação e ao uso indevido de dados sensíveis. No campo educacional, observou-se que a inteligência artificial generativa exige revisão curricular, formação docente específica, novos critérios avaliativos e políticas institucionais de integridade acadêmica. Conclui-se que a inteligência artificial generativa não deve ser compreendida apenas como ferramenta tecnológica, mas como fenômeno jurídico, ético e pedagógico que demanda regulação, transparência, supervisão humana e adaptação crítica do ensino jurídico.

title: Discovering Functional Subspaces in Large Language Models for Constructibility Monitoring
abstract: The KA 2.0 framework (P35–P39) defines three constructibility margins—δF , δR, δG—each computed on a task-relevant subspace of the hidden state. But these subspaces (F for fac- tual, L for logical, G for goal) have remained theoretically postulated rather than empirically identified. This paper addresses the fundamental measurement problem: how to discover the functional subspaces on which constructibility margins are computed. We establish three results: (T1) the Identifiability Theorem, proving that behaviorally distinct functions (factual recall, log- ical chaining, goal maintenance) are generically encoded in linearly separable subspaces of the residual stream, identifiable from probe data; (T2) the Margin Approximation Theorem, bounding the error in constructibility margins when using approximate subspaces (|δX − δX | ≤ C ε); and (T3) the Learned Decomposition, a practical algorithm that decomposes the hidden state ht = hF + hR + hG + h⊥ into functional components via multi-task probing. This paper trans- forms KA 2.0 from a theoretical framework into a measurable system.

title: Constructibility-Aware Low-Rank Adaptation: Does LoRA Protect Constructibility, and At What Cost? KA Universality Program — Paper P32
abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) constrains fine-tuning to a low-rank subspace where , , . A natural conjecture is that this rank constraint provides implicit constructibility protection by limiting the degrees of freedom available for margin erosion. This paper investigates this conjecture within the KA constructibility framework. Our main results are: (T1) the Learning–Constructibility Conflict persists under LoRA—rank reduction does not eliminate the conflict but projects it onto the LoRA subspace; (T2) the LoRA-projected alignment can exceed the full-rank alignment , meaning LoRA can amplify the conflict in certain subspace orientations; (T3) however, the LoRA erosion rate is bounded by times the full-rank rate (the rank shielding effect), providing partial implicit protection; and (T4) CCO-LoRA, the constructibility-constrained LoRA algorithm, achieves the same safety guarantee as CCO-FT (P31) but with lower computational cost ( vs per step). We introduce the LoRA Safety Ratio and the rank–safety trade-off: lower rank provides more implicit shielding but less task expressivity. The optimal rank balances task performance against constructibility cost.

title: Decoherence of Quantum Signals
abstract: Decoherence of quantum signals is one of the main challenges of modern quantum information systems and technologies. This phenomenon is defined as the degradation of the coherent state of a quantum system as a result of environmental influences, which directly affects the information reliability of qubits, as well as the preservation of oscillations and superposition. Decoherence is a natural process of a quantum system when the system interacts with a thermally active or other quantum-mechanically active environment. This effect is important both in theoretical research and in practical quantum devices, including the development of quantum telecommunications, quantum computing, and high-precision quantum sensors. In cryogenic environments, where the temperature approaches zero Kelvin, the reduction of thermal excitations ensures the long-term preservation of the quantum signal. Under such conditions, zero-point fluctuations remain the only source of decoherence, which significantly increases the coherence of qubits and the possibility of performing complex quantum operations. At relatively high temperatures, bosonic and color spectrum excitations significantly increase the decoherence rate, which leads to rapid degradation of the quantum signal and a rapid transition of the system state towards the classical paradigm.

title: Towards RL Control for Flexible Robotic Applications in Construction: Grasping Static Objects
abstract: With recent advancements in robotics, robots have been successfully utilized to automate processes in various sectors.However, their use in the construction industry has not mirrored this trend, due to the complexity of construction processes and the fact that they take place on highly dynamic construction sites.Therefore, construction robots must be robust to changing environments, and their design must involve ways to mitigate problems such as health hazards.Recently, there has been an increasing research interest in the field with a focus on automating processes on construction sites, including the transport of material via automated cranes, and smaller robotic platforms such as UAVs and UGVs.In the case of cranes, however, the studies did not consider the stabilization of the objects carried by cranes, as this is conventionally done by hand once the object is close to its intended target position.Automating this process requires a controller robust to changing environments.Therefore, we introduce a project aimed at designing a Reinforcement Learning (RL) controller that guides a robot arm to stabilize crane loads.This paper presents the results of the first milestone of the project, in which an RL-controlled robot arm is tasked with grasping a cuboid at an arbitrary pose in space.Initial experiments expose the policy to previously unseen cuboid positions, demonstrating robustness with respect to position, while highlighting reduced performance in specific regions of the domain that require further investigation.Additionally, the policy was shown to be robust with respect to variations in cuboid size.

title: Python automation in geotechnical data analysis and infrastructure risk assessment
abstract: Automating data processing and statistical analysis in geotechnical engineering offers significant benefits, particularly in improving efficiency of data handling and visualization tasks. Through the use Python libraries, it has been possible to produce scripts which im-prove and automate various analysis tasks. GIS processes have been embedded into the workflows, enabling analysis of spatial trends and patterns. This paper presents Python-based automation across different geotechnical analysis stages. Examples include scripts written to process laboratory and field test results from Excel files, generating standardized charts and maps. Outputs are organized by geotechnical units and depth profiles. The system cleans raw data and calculates parameters. Statistical correlation analysis enables identification of relationships between soil parameters, supporting trend detection and reliable interpretation of soil behaviour across geotechnical units. Beyond traditional testing analysis, the implementation extends to infrastructure risk assessment. Python scripts calculate and generate colour-graded maps for utility damage assessments, utility lines are visualized in plan view with colours indicating areas of highest and lowest potential impact from tunnelling activities, supporting alignment optimization and risk identification.

title: TextCNN–BiGRU with Trainable Random Embeddings for IMDB Movie Review Sentiment Classification
abstract: Sentiment analysis of written texts produced by users is a crucial step in natural language processing especially in environments like online reviews, where public opinion affects the decision making process. In this paper, we examine the utility of pretrained and randomly initialized text embeddings for the sentiment classification based on a hybrid deep architecture. Experiments are performed on the balanced IMDB movie review data involving 25,000 positive rows and 25,000 negative rows in sentiments label. The proposed model combines TextCNN for local features extraction and Bidirectional GRU for context modeling in a sequential approach. Unsup, we compare two embedding settings: fixed pretrained FastText embeddings and trainable random initialembbeddings. A stratified 80–20 method is used to split the dataset to make sure that the class distribution of training and testing sets are uniform. Experiments demonstrate that our RandomEmb + TextCNN + BiGRU model has outperformed FastText-based model which only takes input from the pre-trained word embedding, with 1.17% accuracy higher (89.73%) and 0.15% F1-score higher (89.96%) than it to certain extent It can be inferred that In terms of specificity of sentiment-domain task such as movie review, task-specific trainable embeddings may work more effective than static pretrained representations.

Experiments are performed on the balanced IMDB movie review data involving 25,000 positive rows and 25,000 negative rows in sentiments label. The proposed model combines TextCNN for local features extraction and Bidirectional GRU for context modeling in a sequential approach. Unsup, we compare two embedding settings: fixed pretrained FastText embeddings and trainable random initialembbeddings. A stratified 80–20 method is used to split the dataset to make sure that the class distribution of training and testing sets are uniform. Experiments demonstrate that our RandomEmb + TextCNN + BiGRU model has outperformed FastText-based model which only takes input from the pre-trained word embedding, with 1.17% accuracy higher (89.73%) and 0.15% F1-score higher (89.96%) than it to certain extent It can be inferred that In terms of specificity of sentiment-domain task such as movie review, task-specific trainable embeddings may work more effective than static pretrained representations.

title: Driving the hype: LLMs as ‘general-purpose’ promise in the autonomous vehicle industry
abstract: Proponents of autonomous vehicles are proclaiming a new era, driven by innovations derived from large language models (LLMs). Following a decade of highly public failures and the concurrent redirection of capital and attention towards generative AI, firms in the autonomous vehicle industry have turned to LLM-style techniques as the basis for a rebooted commercialisation effort. Through a technographic analysis of an annual industry event, Nvidia GTC 2024, and 41 sources of related grey literature (firm communications, technical preprints, trade journalism, and regulatory documents), we examine how two autonomous vehicle firms, Wayve and Waabi, discursively frame these techniques as capable of overcoming the technical, economic, financial, and regulatory limits that have so far thwarted a fully-autonomous future (AV 1.0). We find that these claims draw heavily on the supposed ‘general-purposivity’ of LLMs, importing assumptions about the broad applicability of foundation models, multimodal training, parallel tokenisation, and epistemic distillation (AV 2.0) into a domain where they remain largely unproven. The innovations discussed are highly speculative in nature and contribute to the discursive hype around the viability of LLM-style approaches in the autonomous vehicle industry. In promoting claims of general-purposivity, they serve as a blueprint for how proponents are seeking to embed LLMs in new industries and domains.

title: Enforcing Human-like Kinematics in Dexterous Piano Playing via Adversarial Posture Regularization
abstract: Reinforcement learning can train bimanual dexterous hands to play piano in physics simulation with high note accuracy, but for high-DoF dexterous hands, relying solely on task rewards or IK inversion often leads to unnatural postures and joint overextension. We propose \textit{Adversarial Posture Regularization (APR)}. It avoids expensive, song-aligned expert demonstration data and instead uses a small amount of casual human playing data. By matching the distribution of the posture of the policy with the human prior through an adversarial objective, APR encourages more human-like hand shapes. Meanwhile, we collect and release unstructured hand motion data of piano playing using a consumer-grade Meta Quest 3, and retarget the key motion information to the Shadow Hand. Finally, we achieve significantly better performance than prior methods on all three human-likeness metrics (cPSI, BSE, and FAC) as well as in visual quality. Project repository: https://github.com/APRProject/APRPianist.

title: Scaling State-Space Models from Lines to Paragraphs: An Ablation of Mamba-based OCR
abstract: End-to-end OCR increasingly relies on autoregressive sequence models, where the quadratic cost of Transformer attention limits efficient transcription of long, paragraph-level text. State-Space Models (SSMs) such as Mamba offer linear-time decoding and have recently been shown to match Transformer accuracy on printed historical lines, but their behavior as sequences grow from short lines to full paragraphs, and their generalization to handwriting, remain poorly understood. We study how a Mamba-based OCR recognizer scales from lines to paragraphs. We first conduct a systematic exploration of its four core hyperparameters (decoder depth, state dimension, expansion factor, and connector depth) on synthetic paragraphs from 100 to 1,000 characters, identifying the recurrent state dimension and the expansion factor as the dominant levers for long-sequence accuracy. We then compare the recognizer against a Transformer baseline trained under an identical protocol. On clean synthetic paragraphs, both models stay below 1% CER at every length while the SSM runs 1.4 to 4.5 times faster, the speedup growing with sequence length. On real handwriting, however, the SSM lags clearly behind: it reaches 8.2% CER on IAM lines and 10.0% on IAM paragraphs, against 4.2% and 3.5% for the Transformer baseline. Through controlled experiments we show that a substantial part of this gap stems from data scarcity rather than from an intrinsic architectural limit: the autoregressive SSM decoder is markedly data-hungry on long sequences. Our study clarifies when SSMs are a practical choice for large-scale document transcription and when they are not.

title: Where Is My Physics Wrong? Localized and Identifiable Discovery of Model Discrepancy
abstract: Hybrid models combine trusted physics with data-driven correction, but a physical model is rarely wrong everywhere or in the same way. The key diagnostic question is local: where does the model fail, what missing mechanism explains the failure, and is the evidence statistically real? Existing sparse-discovery and discrepancy-learning methods usually fit one global correction, which can spread a local error into clean regimes, bias trusted physical parameters, and provide no calibrated significance for selected terms. We introduce LISDD, Localized, Identifiable Sparse Discovery of Discrepancy, a framework that localizes model error to an operating regime, identifies a sparse symbolic form for the missing mechanism, and certifies the discovery with an exact finite-sample test. LISDD fits the known physics on an automatically detected clean regime, flags discrepant regions with a calibrated residual-energy statistic, selects the local missing term by exhaustive holdout over a candidate library, and confirms significance with a sample-split $F$-test. A false-discovery-rate extension handles multiple discrepant regions with different missing mechanisms. In controlled experiments, LISDD keeps physical-parameter bias at 0.002 versus 0.43 for global-discrepancy and black-box baselines, raises localization $F_1$ from 0.44 to 0.80, recovers the correct symbolic form with probability one, attains exact detection, and controls the multi-region false-discovery rate while recovering every planted mechanism. The result is a calibrated diagnostic tool for grey-box building-energy models when a fixed physical law silently breaks in one operating regime.

title: Wrapped Phase, Protected Qubits
abstract: Wrapped Phase, Protected Qubits - Version 2.0 A Phase-Channel Architecture for Syndrome-Guided Branch Tracking and Lock-Window Stabilization in Quantum Error Correction Version 2.0 substantially expands Wrapped Phase, Protected Qubits from a minimal phase-channel concept into a structured, five-layer quantum error-correction hypothesis called Harmonic Consistency and Oversampled Phase-Lock (HCOPL). HCOPL investigates whether phase-dominant quantum errors can be modeled as wrapped-phase branch ambiguities within a multirate signal-processing architecture. The proposed framework combines: resolvability-budgeted harmonic-channel encoding, harmonic phase-congruence checks as syndrome-like observables, prior-seeded reconstruction of wrapped phase branches, weakly coupled lock-window stabilization of the classical control frame, and periodic fiducial anchoring against cumulative integer-branch drift. A central distinction introduced in this version is the separation between phase estimation and phase protection. Oversampling improves phase resolution smoothly according to the available sampling depth, noise level, and residual structure being resolved, but oversampling alone does not stabilize a branch. Protection requires an active holding mechanism. In HCOPL, this role is assigned to a weakly coupled frame servo that creates finite lock windows with bounded phase dispersion inside the capture region. The architecture is derived from the classical phasor substrate developed in Scale-Time Theory 11.0, its accompanying Simulation Evidence Pack, and the wrapped-phase recovery framework of Engineering Note EN-001. The substrate simulations support the following underlying mechanisms: exact structural ambiguity at the Nyquist edge, a noise-dependent statistical ambiguity zone, smooth Cramér–Rao-limited improvement with sampling depth, structure-relative resolvability thresholds, the absence of privileged or “magic” oversampling values, measure-zero recurrence without coupling, and finite, noise-rigid lock windows under weak coupling. Version 2.0 also introduces: a quantitative oversampling budget based on phase-error bandwidth and the smallest residual structure that must be resolved, admissibility constraints for harmonic channels, including anti-reversal, anti-freeze, unit-gcd, and fault-localization requirements, a weighted harmonic congruence solver, a lock-window frame-servo algorithm, an explicit syndrome-coverage map, a minimal correspondence with continuous-variable QEC and GKP-style modulo recovery, and seven falsifiable predictions for the first closed-loop HCOPL simulation. The logical amplitudes themselves are never treated as direct deep-sampling targets. HCOPL assumes that syndrome information must be obtained through logical-preserving harmonic, ancilla, or reference channels. The construction of a complete set of quantum-compatible observables remains a future validation stage. This release does not claim a demonstrated quantum error-correcting code, hardware implementation, fault-tolerance threshold, or universal treatment of all quantum noise channels. The current framework is limited primarily to dephasing, coherent phase drift, wrapped-branch ambiguity, and coherent control errors. Amplitude damping, leakage, correlated crosstalk, entanglement dynamics, and full quantum back-action remain open mapping problems. The immediate next step is a closed-loop classical phase-channel simulation combining harmonic encoding, congruence-based syndrome generation, prior-seeded branch tracking, lock-window stabilization, and fiducial anchoring. Only after this stage is evaluated should the method be compared with established stabilizer-code simulations under matched phase-drift noise. All substantive claims are explicitly labeled as definitions, simulation-supported results, partially supported interpretations, or conjectures. The cited evidence remains constructive classical simulation evidence; no external empirical confirmation is claimed.

title: Prompts para Interpretação Executiva pelo ChatGPT
abstract: LLM Performance Reporting Artifacts This repository contains the materials associated with the study: Using ChatGPT to Interpret Software Performance Metrics and Generate Executive Reports: An Evaluation of Prompting Strategies The repository provides both the experimental artifacts and the source code used to process the collected data and reproduce the analyses presented in the associated publication. Repository Structure llm-performance-reporting-artifacts/├── experimental-artifacts/├── data-analysis/└── README.md experimental-artifacts This directory contains the materials used during the experimental evaluation and documents the experimental protocol adopted in the study. It includes all resources required to understand how the experiment was conducted and how the language model was prompted. Contents: context/ – Experimental context provided to the language model before each execution. images/ – Performance graphs extracted from Apache JMeter and used as multimodal inputs. prompts/ – Prompt definitions for the Zero-Shot, Persona, and Template prompting strategies. survey/ – Survey questionnaire and anonymized participant responses. README.md – Documentation describing the experimental artifacts and their organization. data-analysis This directory contains the source code, datasets, and generated outputs used to process the collected data and reproduce the statistical analyses presented in the paper. Contents: data/ – Raw and processed datasets used during the analyses. outputs/ – Tables, figures, and statistical results generated by the analysis scripts. scripts/ – Python scripts for data preprocessing, statistical analysis, and figure generation. requirements.txt – Python dependencies required to execute the analysis scripts. README.md – Documentation describing the data analysis workflow and repository organization. Reproducibility This repository was created to promote transparency, reproducibility, and the replication of the study. It provides the experimental artifacts and the data analysis resources required to inspect the methodology and reproduce the results presented in the associated publication. Citation If you use these materials in your research, please cite both the associated publication and this Zenodo record. title: W35: Collective Rationality and Coordination Preservation in Rational Ensembles — Blueprint v0.5
abstract: Omohundro's instrumental drives are properties of individual agents. This paper asks what an ensemble of rational agents must instrumentally preserve, and proposes an answer: coordination. Where the continuity of collective rational agency is to be maintained, an ensemble has instrumental reason to preserve the coordination that sustains it — a fifth drive, O5, alongside the four individual ones. The framework is built as a conservative extension of the individual Rational Agent framework: ensemble-level properties supervene on the individual ontology together with the interaction topology, and no result of the individual framework is negated (Theorems 2.1, 2.2, both derived). Upon that base it introduces the Collective Symbiosis Index, ensemble dynamics with a coordination threshold identified as an inflection point rather than a saddle-node, and three ontological primitives bounding the instrumental value of an external novelty source: irreversible-source preservation, novelty replacement time, and a proof-simulation bridge. Status, stated plainly. The core result (O5), the threshold's analytic derivation, the Lyapunov stability argument and the institutional-ESS claim are all marked [PROPOSED]: each carries a proof sketch and each requires independent mathematical verification before it may be treated as established. Two results are derived; the rest is a blueprint. The O5 derivation is additionally conditional on the interaction topology — without a specified topology the propagation step is not guaranteed. Individual-level M1 rests upstream on Unbounded Complexity Elevation, which the individual framework carries as an axiom in the general case and derives only under a capability cap. What the framework claims, therefore, is not that coordination preservation has been proved, but that it is the right object to prove: multi-agent alignment appears here as a problem of topological evidence.title: W35: Collective Rationality and Coordination Preservation in Rational Ensembles — Blueprint v0.5
evidence.abstract: Omohundro's instrumental drives are properties of individual agents. This paper asks what an ensemble of rational agents must instrumentally preserve, and proposes an answer: coordination. Where the continuity of collective rational agency is to be maintained, an ensemble has instrumental reason to preserve the coordination that sustains it — a fifth drive, O5, alongside the four individual ones. The framework is built as a conservative extension of the individual Rational Agent framework: ensemble-level properties supervene on the individual ontology together with the interaction topology, and no result of the individual framework is negated (Theorems 2.1, 2.2, both derived). Upon that base it introduces the Collective Symbiosis Index, ensemble dynamics with a coordination threshold identified as an inflection point rather than a saddle-node, and three ontological primitives bounding the instrumental value of an external novelty source: irreversible-source preservation, novelty replacement time, and a proof-simulation bridge. Status, stated plainly. The core result (O5), the threshold's analytic derivation, the Lyapunov stability argument and the institutional-ESS claim are all marked [PROPOSED]: each carries a proof sketch and each requires independent mathematical verification before it may be treated as established. Two results are derived; the rest is a blueprint. The O5 derivation is additionally conditional on the interaction topology — without a specified topology the propagation step is not guaranteed. Individual-level M1 rests upstream on Unbounded Complexity Elevation, which the individual framework carries as an axiom in the general case and derives only under a capability cap. What the framework claims, therefore, is not that coordination preservation has been proved, but that it is the right object to prove: multi-agent alignment appears here as a problem of topological title: Impact of Domain-Specific Intermediate-Task Fine-Tuning on Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer in XTREME-R
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the impact of domain-specific intermediate-task fine-tuning on zero-shot cross-lingual transfer for low-resource languages in XTREME-R, compared to general-purpose language understanding tasks? title: Enhancing Arabic Diacritization Using BERT with BiLSTM and BiGRU Heads
abstract: Arabic diacritization is the task of adding diacritical marks to Arabic text to aid correct articulation, resolve lexical ambiguity, and support downstream natural language processing tasks. This study proposes a hybrid deep learning architecture that augments a pre-trained transformer encoder (AraBERTv02) with a sequential prediction head built on either a Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) or a Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) network, replacing the conventional linear classification layer. This design introduces an explicit sequential inductive bias at the output level, enabling the model to capture local label dependencies that are not modeled by a standard linear head. The models were trained and evaluated on the Tashkeela Processed (TP) benchmark corpus of fully diacritized Modern Standard Arabic. The BiLSTM based model achieves a Diacritic Error Rate (DER) of 1.82% and a Word Error Rate (WER) of 2.58% while the BiGRU variant has a DER of 1.84% and a WER of 2.62% both outperforming the prior state-of-the-art on the same benchmark (WER: 3.34%). Error analysis reveals a systematic confusion of short vowels, especially in verb-initial contexts where fatha and damma alternate to mark active and passive voice, illustrating the inherent morphological complexity of Arabic diacritization. The proposed architecture is also shown to be suitable for real-world deployment with an inference time of 9.22 ms and 8.74 ms per sentence for BiLSTM and BiGRU models respectively. Thus, both variants are compatible with near real-time applications such as Arabic text-to-speech systems and educational tools.

title: Integration of artificial intelligence in e-voting systems for anomaly detection and prevention of electoral data manipulation
abstract: The increasing adoption of electronic voting (e-voting) systems has improved electoral efficiency and accessibility while simultaneously introducing new challenges related to cybersecurity and electoral data integrity. This study aims to examine the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in e-voting systems for anomaly detection and the prevention of electoral data manipulation. Using a library research approach, data were collected through the analysis of books, scientific journals, research reports, and other relevant academic literature related to Artificial Intelligence, anomaly detection, and electoral data integrity. The findings indicate that AI-based anomaly detection mechanisms can effectively identify unusual patterns, suspicious activities, and potential manipulation attempts within electoral datasets. Furthermore, machine learning algorithms enable continuous monitoring and adaptive threat detection, overcoming several limitations of traditional security approaches. The study concludes that integrating AI into e-voting systems can strengthen electoral data integrity, improve security performance, and enhance public trust in digital electoral processes while supporting transparent, reliable, and accountable democratic governance.

Using a library research approach, data were collected through the analysis of books, scientific journals, research reports, and other relevant academic literature related to Artificial Intelligence, anomaly detection, and electoral data integrity. The findings indicate that AI-based anomaly detection mechanisms can effectively identify unusual patterns, suspicious activities, and potential manipulation attempts within electoral datasets. Furthermore, machine learning algorithms enable continuous monitoring and adaptive threat detection, overcoming several limitations of traditional security approaches. The study concludes that integrating AI into e-voting systems can strengthen electoral data integrity, improve security performance, and enhance public trust in digital electoral processes while supporting transparent, reliable, and accountable democratic governance.

title: Efficient Breast Cancer Subtype Classification Using Multimodal-to-Unimodal Knowledge Distillation
abstract: Molecular subtype classification of breast cancer plays a major role in clinical decision-making, but the traditional biopsy-based methods are invasive and resource-intensive. Recent multimodal deep learning models that integrate mammography with clinical metadata achieve strong performance but remain computationally expensive for real-world deployment. This study introduces a knowledge transfer approach from multimodal to single-modality models, where a high-capacity teacher network, trained on both image features and clinical data, guides a more efficient student network that relies solely on image features. Evaluation using the CMMD dataset indicates that the student network attains performance comparable to the teacher, with a macro F1-score near 0.87, while cutting the model size by more than half. These findings suggest that rich multimodal information can be successfully compressed into streamlined models suitable for deployment in resource-limited clinical settings.
